findings.title: M7 states the finite-type geometry of SPEC 2.14 for every board, and its verification for 'every board of rank two to eight'
findings.location: site/src/content/modules/m7-geometry.mdx, route /modules/m7-geometry/: beat 2; beat 6; Seen bullets 1, 2 and 4
findings.claim: M7 drops the finite-type hypothesis that SPEC 2.14 places on its geometry. Beat 2 says 'Free play from the position reaches finitely many positions, its orbit, whose convex hull is a polytope', and Seen 2 says 'The orbit of a position with no negative number is the vertex set of a polytope whose shape depends only on the ringed nodes'. Neither sentence restricts the board, and both are false off the finite types. Beat 6 and Seen 1 and 4 give the verification as 'verified by computation ... every board of rank two to eight'.
findings.expected: SPEC 2.14: 'Euclidean coordinates (finite type)'; the recipe is '[V for every type of rank 2 to 8; oracle function euclidean_basis]'; the Coxeter-plane facts are '[V for every type of rank 2 to 8]'. SPEC 0.3: the range of boards checked is part of the claim. SPEC 2.7: 'Finite type means one of the boards of section 2.8'. Precedents: round 1 P3-RT-09-02 and P3-RT-09-07.
findings.observed: On the triangle A2~ (rank 3, roads both ways, affine by classify), free play from (1,0,0) passes 5000 positions (engine orbit truncated; oracle orbit(..., cap=5000) raises OverflowError). The orbit is infinite, so it is the vertex set of no polytope. On the same board the form is singular ((1,1,1) has form value 0; eigenvalues of D^1/2 C D^-1/2 are 0, 3, 3), there is no Coxeter number and no Coxeter plane, and the engine's euclideanBasis throws NotFiniteType. Nothing in 2.14 was verified there. golden types[T].coxeter_plane covers the 31 finite types of rank 2 to 8 only.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run --project site-unit site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-09-p4-m7-finite-type.test.ts. Result: test 1 passes (the five sentences are on the page and beat 2 never says 'finite type'); tests 2 and 3 fail (orbit truncated at 5000 on the triangle; euclideanBasis throws NotFiniteType). Oracle: python3 redteam/RT-09/redteam-RT-09-p4-oracle.py reference (lines M7-b6-triangle, M7-b2-triangle-orbit, INFO M7-triangle). Preview build.
findings.specRef: SPEC 2.14 (Euclidean coordinates '(finite type)'; '[V for every type of rank 2 to 8]'); 2.7 opening; 0.3; lens attacks 1, 25 and 29. Oracle: cartan_class(triangle)='affine'; orbit(triangle, [(1,0,0)], fire, cap=5000) raises OverflowError.
findings.proposedFix: Add 'on a board of finite type' to beat 2 and Seen 2. In beat 6 and Seen 1 and 4, write 'on every board of finite type of rank two to eight'.

findings.title: M6's Seen box gives the root lengths of the finite types B, C, F, G for every balanced board: 'short roots have form value 2, long ones 4 or 6'
findings.claim: The bullet reads: 'Exactly the balanced boards have a form with positive city weights that no mutation changes ([W20], Theorems 8.4, 8.7); short roots have form value 2, long ones 4 or 6, verified by computation.' The first clause sets the scope to balanced boards, and the length statement keeps that scope with no restriction to the finite types. It is false on balanced boards that the site itself offers (T15, T16).

Off them a balanced board can have other lengths, and more than two (SPEC 2.12 twisted table, column 'weights d'). Lens attack 1. Precedent: round 1 P3-RT-09-02.

Test 1 passes (the bullet is on the page); tests 2 and 3 fail with form values 2, 8 on A2^(2) and 2, 4, 8 on A4^(2). Oracle: python3 redteam/RT-09/redteam-RT-09-p4-oracle.py reference (INFO M6-seen2-*). Preview build.

findings.title: M7's b12 challenge rejects a right answer: the rings (2, 1, 0) on B3 give 24 vertices and 36 edges, but the check accepts only (1, 1, 0)
findings.location: site/src/content/modules/m7-geometry.mdx, Challenge for b12 (route /modules/m7-geometry/); check { kind: 'out', name: 'polytopeName', equals: 'truncated octahedron' }
findings.claim: The goal is 'Find rings on B3, other than those of beat 5, that also give 24 vertices and 36 edges.' The check reads T10's polytopeName. T10 names a polytope only for the exact rings of a golden wythoff record (t10/names.ts POLYTOPE_NAMES, keyed by '<type>:<rings>'), so the check is met by (1, 1, 0) alone (decisions/P4-A6.md: 'the name check is met only by B3 (1, 1, 0)'). Rings such as (2,1,0) or (1,2,0) satisfy the goal as printed, and M7 itself says the shape 'depends only on which nodes are ringed'. The challenge never reports success for them.
findings.expected: SPEC 4.0 Predict and 8.5 (a challenge 'says when its goal is reached'); lens attack 16 ('reach the goal by a legitimate play and by a near miss, and read whether the check reports success'). SPEC 2.14: 'whose combinatorics depend only on which nodes are ringed'. Oracle: wythoff_f_vector(cartan('B',3), [2,1,0]) = [24, 36, 14, 1], the same as for [1,1,0].
findings.observed: On the built page, b12 was played from (0,1,1) to (1,1,1), then (2,1,1) (Ring 1 up), then (2,1,0). It showed vertexCount 24, edgeCount 36, fVector '24, 36, 14' and edgeLengths '4, 16'. The challenge's data-met stayed null and no 'Goal reached.' appeared. Control: (0,1,1) to (0,1,0) to (1,1,0) gives polytopeName 'truncated octahedron' and data-met='true'.
findings.reproduction:
npm ci --prefer-offline; npm run build; copy playwright.config.ts with a free port and the webServer command `node ../node_modules/astro/bin/astro.mjs preview --port

--ignore-lock` in site/. Then PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH= npx playwright test -c site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-09-p4-m7-b12-challenge.spec.ts. The first test fails (data-met null after (2,1,0) with 24 vertices and 36 edges); the control test passes. A copy outside the repository needs NODE_PATH=/node_modules. Preview build.
findings.specRef: SPEC 8.5; 4.0 Predict; 2.14 (orbit polytopes); lens attack 16. Golden wythoff[type=B3;rings=1,1,0].f_vector = [24, 36, 14].
findings.proposedFix: Check the property the goal names: fVector equal to '24, 36, 14', with the board B3 and node 3 unringed. Or word the goal as 'ring the nodes, one ring each, ...' so that only (1,1,0) answers it.

findings.title: M7 says 'make uniform' replays from (0, 1, √2); the studio replays from (0, 1/√2, 1), and its own edge-length readout contradicts the caption
findings.location: site/src/content/modules/m7-geometry.mdx, beat 5 ('replaying the same moves from (0,1,\sqrt2) in floating point') and the b7 caption ('redraws it from (0, 1, √2) with one edge length'); site/src/components/tools/t10/uniform.ts (uniformStart, c = largest ringed integer)
findings.claim: The lesson tells the reader which real start the studio uses. T10 uses a_i = c/sqrt(d_i) with c = 1, which is (0, 1/sqrt2, 1) on B3. That is (0,1,sqrt2)/sqrt2, so the drawn polytope is the uniform truncated cube at another scale, not the orbit of (0,1,sqrt2).
findings.expected: SPEC 2.14: the squared length of the edge from lambda to R_i lambda is 2 d_i a_i^2, which from (0,1,sqrt2) on B3 (d = (2,2,1)) is 4 at both ringed nodes. SPEC 4 T10, Make uniform: 'a_i = c/sqrt(d_i)'. The caption must state what the figure shows (4.0 'Starts meaningful'; lens attack 25, 'a drawn object that contradicts its caption').
findings.observed: On the built page, M7 b7 with make uniform on shows uniform 'on' and edgeLengths '2' (squared length 2 at the start), not 4.
findings.reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c <copy of playwright.config.ts on a free port> site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-09-p4-m7-uniform.spec.ts. It fails with 'the studio reads "2"' where (0,1,√2) gives 4. Preview build.
findings.specRef: SPEC 2.14 Edge lengths ('the uniform truncated cube is B3 with numbers (0,1,sqrt2)'); 4 T10 Make uniform; decisions/P4-A3.md (make uniform, c = largest ring). Oracle: 2*symmetrizer(cartan('B',3))[1]*1^2 = 4. Graded major, not blocker: the shape (a uniform truncated cube) is as stated and only the stated start vector is wrong. Lens attack 25 would grade it blocker.
findings.proposedFix: Say 'from a multiple of (0, 1, √2)' or 'from (0, 1/√2, 1)', or take c so that the start is (0, 1, √2) on this configuration.

findings.title: M6 quotes Donnelly's theorem on the forms fired without saying that his matrix is the transpose of the site's
findings.location: site/src/content/modules/m6-multiple-edges.mdx: beat 4 ('... x_2: the positive roots of the reversed board [Don08] (Theorem 5.2)') and Seen bullet 3 ('Firing is mutation on the reversed board, transposed. Verified by computation; [Don08].')
findings.claim: The quoted result turns on which board is 'reversed', and in Donnelly's convention the matrix is C^T. The M6 page never states this. M5, which quotes the same theorem, does: 'Donnelly fires positive numbers, as this site does; his matrix is the transpose of the Cartan matrix used here.'
findings.expected: SPEC 8.4: 'State the convention whenever a result is quoted from a source that uses another one (section 2.9)'. SPEC 2.9: 'Donnelly [Don08] ... a = lambda, C = M^T'. Lens attack 22: a quoted statement true as printed but with no convention is major.
findings.observed: M6 contains neither 'Donnelly' nor any statement that M = C^T. The statement is true in the site's convention, verified by oracle symbolic_play(cartan('B',2), [0,1,0,1]) = (1,0), (2,1), (1,1), (0,1).
findings.reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run --project site-unit site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-09-p4-m6-donnelly-convention.test.ts. Test 1 passes (M5 states the convention); test 2 fails (M6 quotes [Don08] and never states it). Preview build.
findings.specRef: SPEC 8.4; 2.9 (Donnelly row); F6; lens attack 22. RT-08 attack 31 covers the same rule from the wording side, so the two reports should be merged.
findings.proposedFix: Add M5's sentence after the [Don08] citation in beat 4.

findings.title: M6 beat 1 sets B2 against 'every road had a road back', but B2 is bidirected and M3 already showed a one-way road
findings.claim: 'Until now every road had a road back, as on A2. Here the one-way counts of two cities, the numbers of roads each way, differ ...' In SPEC 2.1's words this contrast says that B2 has a road with no road back, which would make it a one-way board. It is not one. The opening clause is also not so: M3 beat 6 played on a single road with none back.
findings.expected: SPEC 2.1: a board is bidirected when 'every road has at least one road back'; B2 (two roads from 1 to 2 and one back) is bidirected. 'Two roads one way, one back' is the intended contrast with 'one road each way'.
findings.observed: B2: adjacency has A_12 = 2 and A_21 = 1 (boardKind 'gcm'). M3 contains 'Take a single road from city 1 to city 2 and none back.'
findings.reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run --project site-unit site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-09-p4-m6-road-back.test.ts. Test 1 passes (the sentence is on the page); tests 2 and 3 fail.
findings.specRef: SPEC 2.1 (bidirected, one-way board); Appendix C; M3 beat 6.
findings.proposedFix: Write 'Until now every road was matched by exactly one road back, as on A2.'
